otoscope.context: A handheld otoscope with a grip handle and a cone-shaped tip for looking into the ear. Used for ear exams, ENT clinics, pediatric checkups and ear infection information.

ophthalmoscope.context: A handheld ophthalmoscope with a slim handle and a flat head with a small viewing hole. Used for eye examinations, optometry, retina checks and medical training material.

reflex-hammer.context: A reflex hammer with a triangular rubber head on a thin handle. Used for neurological exams, knee jerk tests, physical checkups and neurology content.

tuning-fork.context: A tuning fork with two long prongs and a short stem. Doctors use it for hearing tests and vibration sense checks, and it also stands for pitch and sound in music.

penlight.context: A slim medical penlight with a pocket clip, shining light from its tip. Used for pupil checks, throat exams, nursing supplies and first-aid kits.

head-mirror.context: A doctor's head mirror: a round mirror with a centre hole mounted on a headband. It is the classic sign of an ear, nose and throat doctor and appears in ENT clinic and old-style doctor imagery.

pulse-oximeter.context: A fingertip pulse oximeter clipped onto a finger, its screen showing a pulse wave. Used for oxygen saturation readings, vital signs, home health monitoring and respiratory care.

lancing-device.context: A pen-shaped lancing device with a drop of blood at its tip. Used for finger-prick blood sugar tests, diabetes care apps and home testing instructions.

urine-dipstick.context: A urine test strip with a row of square reagent pads. Used for urinalysis, lab tests, home test kits, pregnancy and kidney health information.

peak-flow-meter.context: A peak flow meter: a tube with a mouthpiece and a slider on its scale. Used for asthma action plans, lung function checks and respiratory care apps.

spirometer.context: A handheld spirometer with a screen and a sideways mouthpiece tube. Used for lung function tests, respiratory clinics, COPD and asthma care.

incentive-spirometer.context: An incentive spirometer: an upright cylinder with a piston and a hose to a mouthpiece. Used for deep breathing exercises after surgery, respiratory therapy and hospital discharge guides.

holter-monitor.context: A Holter monitor box with three wires to round electrode pads. Used for 24 hour heart rhythm recording, cardiology referrals and arrhythmia information.

ecg-electrode.context: A round ECG electrode pad with a scalloped adhesive edge and a snap stud in the middle. Used in heart monitoring, medical supply catalogues and patient preparation guides.

defibrillator-pads.context: Two defibrillator pads marked with lightning bolts, their wires joined to one plug. Used for AED training, first aid guides, CPR courses and emergency equipment signs.

ear-thermometer.context: An ear thermometer with a short cone probe and a small screen. Used for taking temperature at home, fever checks for children and pharmacy product listings.

fetal-doppler.context: A fetal doppler unit showing a heart on its screen, with a cable to a round probe. Used for listening to a baby's heartbeat in pregnancy, antenatal care and midwife apps.

pinard-horn.context: A Pinard horn, the trumpet-shaped fetal stethoscope with an earpiece disc. Midwives use it to listen to a baby's heartbeat, and it appears in midwifery and maternity care content.

dermatoscope.context: A dermatoscope with a round magnifying lens ringed by small lights on a handle. Used for skin exams, mole checks, dermatology clinics and skin cancer screening.

laryngoscope.context: A laryngoscope with a straight handle and a curved blade. Used for intubation, anesthesia, emergency airway management and medical training.

audiometer.context: Hearing test headphones with a hand response button on a cord. Used for hearing screenings, audiology clinics, audiogram results and workplace hearing checks.

stadiometer.context: A height measuring rod with tick marks and a headpiece resting on a person's head. Used for measuring height in clinics, growth checks, school nurses and fitness assessments.

hand-dynamometer.context: A hand grip dynamometer with a round dial gauge above a D-shaped grip. Used for grip strength tests in physiotherapy, occupational therapy, rehab and fitness assessment.

goniometer.context: A goniometer: a round protractor disc with two long hinged arms. Physiotherapists use it to measure joint angles and range of motion in rehab and orthopedic assessments.

neuro-pinwheel.context: A neurological pinwheel with a spiked wheel on a pen handle. Neurologists roll it over the skin to test sensation, and it appears in neurology exam content.

baby-scale.context: An infant weighing scale with a baby lying in a curved cradle tray on a low base. Used for newborn weigh-ins, pediatric clinics, baby growth trackers and maternity wards.

pain-scale.context: A pain scale with a happy face and a sad face above a graded bar. Used for rating pain, symptom trackers, patient questionnaires and nursing assessments.

growth-chart.context: A growth chart with percentile curves fanning out and one plotted point. Used for tracking child height and weight, pediatric checkups and baby growth apps.

breathalyzer.context: A breathalyzer with a screen and a straight mouthpiece tube on top. Used for breath alcohol tests, drink driving information, police and workplace testing.

capsule-endoscope.context: A pill camera: a capsule with a clear dome lens and a camera eye sending out light. Used for capsule endoscopy, digestive health information and gastroenterology services.

phoropter.context: A phoropter, the wide eye test device with two round lens windows on a mount. Used for eye tests, refraction, optician and optometrist services.

sonogram.context: An ultrasound printout with a fan-shaped scan showing a curled baby. Used for pregnancy announcements, baby scan appointments, prenatal care and maternity apps.

lab-report.context: A lab report sheet with a small test tube at the top and rows of results, one of them flagged. Used for blood test results, patient portals, pathology and diagnostics.

mri-scanner.context: An MRI scanner: a large square housing with a round bore and a patient table sliding out. Used for MRI appointments, radiology departments and imaging services.

ct-scanner.context: A CT scanner: an upright ring gantry with a patient table sliding through the centre. Used for CT scan appointments, radiology departments and emergency imaging.

x-ray-machine.context: An X-ray machine with a tube head on a column arm above a patient table. Used for radiography departments, X-ray appointments and imaging services.

c-arm.context: A C-arm X-ray unit: a large C-shaped arm on a wheeled base. Used in operating rooms, fluoroscopy, interventional radiology and orthopedic surgery.

ultrasound-machine.context: An ultrasound machine: a cart with a screen showing a scan fan, a console and wheels. Used for sonography departments, scan appointments and hospital equipment lists.

ultrasound-probe.context: An ultrasound probe with a narrow grip and a wide curved face sending out sound waves. Used for sonography, scan appointments and point of care ultrasound.

lead-apron.context: A lead X-ray apron with a radiation symbol on the chest. Used for radiation protection signs, radiology staff safety and X-ray room rules.

dosimeter-badge.context: A radiation dosimeter badge with a clip, a radiation symbol and a reading window. Worn by radiology and nuclear workers to track radiation dose.

oxygen-mask.context: An oxygen face mask over the nose and mouth with a strap and a tube. Used for oxygen therapy, respiratory care, emergency care and airplane safety information.

nebulizer.context: A nebulizer: a small compressor box with a tube to a mask and medicine cup. Used for asthma and COPD breathing treatments, home care and respiratory therapy.

inhaler-spacer.context: An inhaler spacer chamber with a mouthpiece at one end and an inhaler fitted at the other. Used for asthma action plans, children's inhaler technique and pharmacy advice.

nasal-cannula.context: A nasal cannula: a tube loop with two short prongs for the nose. Used for oxygen therapy, home oxygen, hospital care and respiratory information.

oxygen-concentrator.context: A home oxygen concentrator on wheels with a handle and tubing. Used for home oxygen therapy, COPD care, medical equipment rental and respiratory support.

oxygen-flowmeter.context: A wall oxygen flowmeter: a clear tube with a floating ball, a knob on top and a nozzle below. Used in hospital rooms for setting oxygen flow and in respiratory care guides.

suction-unit.context: A medical suction unit: a gauge piped to a canister jar with a hanging tube. Used for airway suction in hospitals, ambulances and emergency equipment lists.

bag-valve-mask.context: A manual resuscitator: an oval squeeze bag joined through a valve to a face mask. Used for CPR and rescue breathing training, emergency medicine and ambulance equipment.

pocket-mask.context: A CPR pocket mask with a one-way valve port in the centre. Used for first aid and CPR training, rescue breathing and first-aid kit contents.

oropharyngeal-airway.context: An oral airway: a curved plastic tube with a flat flange at the straight end. Used for keeping an airway open in first aid, emergency medicine and anesthesia.

endotracheal-tube.context: A breathing tube: a long curved tube with an inflated cuff near the tip and a connector at the top. Used for intubation, ventilators, anesthesia and intensive care.

tracheostomy-tube.context: A tracheostomy tube: a winged neck plate with a short curved tube. Used for tracheostomy care, long-term ventilation, ICU and airway information.

insulin-pen.context: An insulin pen with a dose dial, a cartridge window and a short needle. Used for diabetes care, insulin reminders, pharmacy and injection instructions.

insulin-pump.context: An insulin pump with a screen and buttons, tubing leading out of the top. Used for diabetes technology, insulin therapy and type 1 diabetes apps.

cgm-sensor.context: A continuous glucose sensor: a round skin patch with a drop symbol sending a wireless signal. Used for diabetes apps, blood sugar tracking and wearable health devices.

auto-injector.context: An emergency auto-injector pen with a safety cap and a rounded tip. Used for severe allergy action plans, anaphylaxis training and school first-aid information.

pacemaker.context: A pacemaker: a rounded metal case with a lead wire running to a heart. Used for cardiology information, heart rhythm treatment and implant warnings near equipment.

stent.context: A coronary stent: a short mesh tube with a diamond lattice. Used for angioplasty information, heart and artery treatment and cardiology services.

cochlear-implant.context: A cochlear implant: an ear with a round coil above it joined by a wire to a sound processor. Used for deaf and hard of hearing services, audiology and accessibility content.

hip-implant.context: A hip replacement implant: a metal stem with a ball head in a round cup. Used for orthopedic surgery information, joint replacement and physiotherapy content.

bone-plate.context: An orthopedic bone plate: a waisted metal strip with a row of screw holes. Used for fracture fixation, orthopedic surgery and trauma care information.

bone-screw.context: An orthopedic bone screw with a wide flat head and deep coarse threads. Used for fracture fixation, orthopedic surgery, dental and trauma implant information.
